problem: Given that ${x}_{1}$ and ${x}_{2}$ are the solutions of the equation $\operatorname{cos}⁡x=\frac{1}{4}$ for $0\le x<2\pi ,$ what is the value of ${x}_{1}\cdot {x}_{2}$ to the nearest integer?

feedback.worked_solution:
First, we find the principal value:

$$
\begin{aligned}x=\operatorname{arccos}⁡(\frac{2}{7})=1.281\,044…≈1.2810\end{aligned}
$$

Since $1.2810$ lies inside the specified domain, our first solution, rounded to one decimal place, is $x=1.3.$

Our first solution lies in the first quadrant and has a reference angle of ${\theta }_{R}=1.2810.$ Since $\operatorname{cos}⁡x>0,$ the second solution must lie in the fourth quadrant, and it also has a reference angle ${\theta }_{R}=1.2810.$

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/13952163/assets/1b1b50c4d13ebae81a4c8af45ec2c9fde8dc6810da78bd21f74ebcdd117a375e.png)

Since the second solution $x$ lies in the $4$th quadrant, we can find it using the reference angle as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}x & =2\pi -{\theta }_{R} \\  & =2\pi -1.2810 \\  & ≈5.0022 \\  & ≈5.0\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, arranged in ascending order, the solutions are $x=1.3$ and $x=5.0.$
